title: Three fusion companies in DOE’s Milestone program have updates
summary: Three U.S. companies participating in the Department of Energy’s public-private Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program recently have reported new developments. Xcimer Energy, Zap Energy, and Commonwealth Fusion Systems are among the eight companies that the DOE selected in 2023 to develop fusion pilot plant designs and resolve related scientific and technological challenges within 5–10 years. The goal of the Milestone Program is to accelerate privately funded fusion companies toward commercial viability with the assistance of targeted public-private investment that is linked to independently verified technical and commercial “milestones.”

title: Chernobyl updates: Stable fuel particles, solid waste disposal
summary: More than 40 years after the meltdown of Unit 4 at Ukraine’s Chernobyl nuclear power plant, research into radioactive material at the site continues, as do efforts toward cleanup and decommissioning. In a paper published in the March 2026 issue of the Journal of Hazardous Materials and disseminated widely last week, a team of researchers from the Leibniz University Hannover and Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf research laboratory revealed that the fuel components of six “hot particles”—pieces of radioactive debris resulting from the Chernobyl explosion—appeared structurally stable, with the fissile material bound within the particles.

title: Bangladesh’s Rooppur-1 Nuclear Plant Achieves First Criticality
summary: Unit 1 at the Rooppur nuclear power station being built by Russia in Bangladesh has achieved criticality with grid connection expected by the end of November. The 1,080-MW VVER V-523 pressurised water reactor unit, construction of which began in 2017, achieved first criticality at 15:34 on 11 October. First criticality is the milestone moment when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining, controlled chain reaction for the very first time. Rooppur, Bangladesh’s most expensive infrastructure facility, has considerable backing from Russia. Moscow is financing $11.9bn (€10.6bn) in state loans for the project, which has been estimated to cost up to $12.8bn.
